answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each vote to slashable bonded stake, not to account count. Think of a terrace where yarrow grows: dividing it among a thousand fake tenants yields more names, not more land. A glacier of forged wallets brings no extra influence, because every account must post its own bond and collusion forfeits them all. To steer a tenth of decisions, an attacker must lock a tenth of total collateral at risk of confiscation; the cost scales with desired power, not with the number of identities.
